reader.requirement: At --std 85, a level-01 data-name in the File or Working-Storage Section, a file-name, or a report-name described with GLOBAL must be a global name, and so must every data-name subordinate to it (any level, including the records of a GLOBAL FD and items in an OCCURS table) and every condition-name associated with it or with a subordinate; names of a non-GLOBAL entry (01, its subordinates and 88s, a 77) stay local; GLOBAL is admitted only where X.4.6.3 SR1 allows it (not in LINKAGE, not below level 01, not on a 77).

edition-consulted.switches: construct linkage-global-2002: the GLOBAL clause in the LINKAGE SECTION is refused below 2002 (COBOL0900)

reader.edition-search: read InheritContainerGlobalData/InheritGlobalSubtree and InheritStep's root gathering; grep LinkageGlobal2002 and the Constructs/ConstructRegistry tables for GLOBAL (only linkage-global-2002); DataBinder.ClausePlacement.cs's GLOBAL placement (COBOL2404) has no edition test. The inheritance of the subtree consults no edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: GLOBAL in the LINKAGE SECTION is refused at 85 and admitted from 2002; the global-name propagation to subordinates and condition-names is the same code at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers a GLOBAL FD's several records and their subordinates and GLOBAL REDEFINES entries from direct and indirect containees; not exercised: condition-names (on the 01, on a subordinate, in an OCCURS table), a GLOBAL record of a non-GLOBAL FD, subordinates of a table with an index-name, edited and scaled signed subordinates, the locality of a non-GLOBAL record's names, and the SR1 placement refusals at 85. All probed here.

citations.check: OK  §1985:X.4.6.4 GR1  (║4.6.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: InheritGlobalSubtree makes the whole subtree of each container GLOBAL root visible (children, condition-names, index-names, level-66 entries) and leaves non-GLOBAL roots out. One reading to flag, not a failure: the 66 RENAMES of a GLOBAL record is inherited as global; the 1985 text names subordinates and condition-names only, but §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR3 qualifies data-name-1 only by its 01, so treating it as part of the global record is a defensible reading the text does not refute.

refuter.evidence: gs1.cob (run gs1-002, --std 85; the first run gs1-001 was my own error, CF FINAL without CONTROL FINAL, correctly refused COBOL0899): GLOBAL RD R-1 with a CF FINAL sum counter S-TOT SUM WAMT, and WS '01 GE IS GLOBAL IS EXTERNAL' with a signed scaled SIGN LEADING SEPARATE subordinate and an 88 range. The containee printed 'D S-TOT=0012 / D S-TOT OF R-1=0012 / D GE-BIG +150.5'. A data-name subordinate to a GLOBAL report-name (the sum counter, unqualified and qualified by the report-name) is a global name, and the condition-name of a GLOBAL EXTERNAL record's subordinate is global. The report printed '07 / 05 / 0012'. gs2.cob (gs2-002, compile only): the same with a non-GLOBAL RD. The containee's 'MOVE S-TOT2' is refused with COBOL1639 'not defined' and 'GENERATE DET-2' with COBOL1757: the names of a non-GLOBAL report stay local. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:X.4.6.4 GR1 ... the text is in GR1'; 'OK  §1985:X.4.6.3 SR1 ... the text is in SR1'.
